name: Augustus
title: The first emperor of the Roman Empire
summary: Augustus (Gaius Octavius), also known as Caesar Augustus, was the first emperor of the Roman Empire. He is known in the Bible for issuing the decree for a census that led Joseph and Mary to travel to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born. His reign marked the beginning of the Pax Romana, a period of peace that facilitated the spread of the gospel.

keyEvents.title: The Decree for the Census
keyEvents.description: Augustus issued a decree that all the Roman world should be registered in a census. This decree directly led Joseph and Mary to travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Jesus during the Reign of Augustus
keyEvents.description: During the reign of Emperor Augustus, Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem in Judea, an event that fulfilled Micah's prophecy about the birthplace of the Messiah.

keyEvents.title: Herod the Great as a Vassal King
keyEvents.description: Augustus appointed and maintained Herod the Great as a client king over Judea. Herod's reign under Augustus' sovereignty forms the political framework for Jesus' birth.

keyEvents.title: Pax Romana and the Spread of the Gospel
keyEvents.description: Augustus' establishment of peace and stability in the Roman Empire, with good roads and a common language, laid the practical foundation for the later spread of Christianity throughout the empire.

keyEvents.title: The Roman Taxation
keyEvents.description: Augustus' system of taxation and census affected daily life throughout the empire, including in Judea and Galilee, and is the background for several New Testament accounts.
